# Master techniques

There are 16 Sword Masters, one for each breathing method. Each one fights with its own set of named techniques: 417 in all. A technique is one to four strikes. Each strike has a **wind-up** (the Master's tell) and a **shape**, and the shape tells you how to get out of the way.

Your **first clear** of a Master teaches you its technique part, once. Several Masters teach the same part (for example Bind), so a later clear of another one may only record the win.

## Reading a strike

| Shape | What you see | Your answer |
|---|---|---|
| Broad cut | A wide sweeping cut in front | Back off or guard (step out of reach) |
| Low sweep | The blade sweeps along the ground | Jump |
| High sweep | The blade cuts at head height | Crouch |
| Line | A thrust, lunge, cleave or other straight cut along one narrow lane | Sidestep out of the lane |
| Circle | A whirl, or any strike thrown spinning | Leave the circle (step out of the radius) |

In the tables below every strike is named, and the **Answers** column gives the answer for each strike in order.

**Heavy** strikes wind up longer and hit harder. **Quick** strikes wind up faster and hit lighter. A strike *with a step in* closes distance first, so standing just out of reach is not enough. After the last strike the Master needs a moment to **recover**: that is your opening to hit back.

**Pace.** Each school has its own pace, shown under its name: how long each wind-up takes, and how long the Master stays open after.

**Base damage** is the whole technique if every strike lands, in health points (2 points is one heart), before your defence and elemental match-ups. One technique can never deal more than 1.75 times a single hit. Masters on Stone's footing hit 10% harder.
